questions.prompt: A settled soil sample forms layers 5 cm sand, 3 cm silt and 2 cm clay. Treat layer depth as proportional to fraction quantity for this classroom estimate. Calculate each percentage and explain one limitation of inferring field drainage from these readings alone.
questions.answer: Total depth = 10 cm. Sand is 50%, silt 30% and clay 20%. Field drainage also depends on structure, compaction, organic matter and other conditions; settling behaviour may not perfectly represent particle mass fractions.
questions.explanation: The proportional-depth assumption is explicit. Do not require a precise soil-texture class without a classification triangle or rule.

The only planned nitrogen source is fertiliser containing 20% nitrogen by mass. Calculate the required nitrogen and corresponding fertiliser mass. Ignore other nutrient sources.
questions.answer: Nitrogen requirement = 0.4×60 = 24 kg. At 20% nitrogen, fertiliser mass = 24/0.20 = 120 kg.
questions.explanation: Use the stated assessment and assumptions; the figures are invented practice data and are not a general application recommendation.

markingGuide.description: Calculate 24 kg nitrogen for the field.
Convert 20% to a mass fraction and divide appropriately.

questions.prompt: A germination test of 100 seeds produces 84 normal seedlings, 8 abnormal seedlings and 8 ungerminated seeds. Using normal seedlings as the criterion, calculate germination percentage. Estimate how many seeds would be needed for an expected 420 normal seedlings at that rate, and explain why field establishment may differ.
questions.answer: Germination percentage = 84%. Expected seed requirement = 420/0.84 = 500. Field establishment can differ because of moisture, temperature, pests, planting depth and losses after germination. The estimate is an expectation, not a guarantee for each lot of 500.
questions.explanation: Normal seedlings, not all seeds showing any growth, define the stated criterion.

markingGuide.description: Calculate 84%.

questions.prompt: A monitoring protocol says intervention should be considered when at least 30% of sampled plants show a specified pest damage. A representative sample has 20 damaged plants out of 100 and many natural enemies. Explain the threshold result and two sensible next management steps without assuming a particular chemical treatment.
questions.answer: Observed damage is 20%, below the stated 30% threshold. Continue representative monitoring and confirm the pest, crop stage and damage trend. questions.explanation: Apply the hypothetical threshold and evidence; no real pesticide, dose or universal threshold is recommended.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science

questions.prompt: A farm enterprise earns ₦300,000 revenue, incurs ₦180,000 variable cost and ₦50,000 fixed cost. Calculate gross margin and net profit under these definitions. If revenue falls by 10% while costs stay unchanged, calculate the new net profit and explain the risk shown.
questions.answer: Gross margin = 300,000−180,000 = ₦120,000. Net profit = 120,000−50,000 = ₦70,000. New revenue = ₦270,000 and new net profit = ₦40,000. A 10% revenue fall reduces profit by ₦30,000, illustrating sensitivity when costs do not adjust.
questions.explanation: Distinguish gross margin from net profit and use the stated unchanged-cost assumption.

questions.answer: assembly-language instructions into machine-code representation.
questions.explanation: An assembler operates on assembly language rather than serving as a word processor or database form.
options: Machine-code instructions back into high-level source code.
Spreadsheet formulas directly into paper layout settings.
A complete high-level program as its defining source language.
assembly-language instructions into machine-code representation.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.learningObjective: Explain computer components and data representation.
questions.prompt: Which task is normally part of an operating system’s role?
questions.answer: Manage memory and coordinate running processes.
questions.explanation: The operating system manages resources and provides services to applications.
options: Replace every hardware component physically.
Determine the truth of every web page.
Manage memory and coordinate running processes.
Write every student’s essay automatically as its defining function.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.learningObjective: Apply application concepts to defined tasks.
questions.prompt: A spreadsheet formula =B2*C2 is copied one row down using ordinary relative references. What does the copied formula become?
questions.explanation: Both row references move down by one while the columns remain the same.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.learningObjective: Apply application concepts to defined tasks.
questions.prompt: Which reference keeps both its row and column fixed when a spreadsheet formula is copied?
questions.explanation: Dollar signs before both column and row make both components absolute in the stated common spreadsheet notation.
options: F1

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.learningObjective: Apply application concepts to defined tasks.
questions.prompt: Why is a unique student admission number a suitable primary key for a student table?
questions.answer: It can identify each student record without relying on names being unique.
questions.explanation: A key distinguishes records; two students can legitimately have the same name.
options: It must contain the student’s complete address.
It guarantees that every other field is correct.
It is needed only for choosing font colour.
It can identify each student record without relying on names being unique.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.learningObjective: Apply application concepts to defined tasks.
questions.prompt: Which database operation most directly returns records whose class field equals “SS1”?
questions.answer: A query with the appropriate selection condition.
questions.explanation: A selection query filters records according to criteria.
options: A data-entry form used only to add new rows.
A report-layout change with no selection criteria.
A query with the appropriate selection condition.
An import of every record without filtering.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.learningObjective: Distinguish communication functions and diagnose simple faults.
questions.prompt: A school connects computers within its own nearby buildings for shared services. This is most naturally described as
questions.answer: a local area network.
questions.explanation: LAN describes a local network scope rather than a guarantee about public internet access.
options: a storage file extension.
a local area network.
the entire World Wide Web by definition.
an international satellite system only.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.learningObjective: Distinguish communication functions and diagnose simple faults.
questions.prompt: What is the main role of a router in an ordinary IP network?
questions.answer: Forward packets between networks according to routing information.
questions.explanation: A router connects network paths; it is distinct from a document editor or a passive cable.
options: Forward packets between networks according to routing information.
Forward frames only within a local segment using MAC addresses as its defining role.
Resolve hostnames as its defining routing operation.
Allocate spreadsheet cell formats to network addresses.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.learningObjective: Distinguish communication functions and diagnose simple faults.
questions.prompt: A browser knows a website’s hostname but needs an IP address for a connection. Which service commonly supplies the name-to-address information?
questions.answer: DNS.
questions.explanation: The Domain Name System supports hostname resolution; it does not itself prove that a site’s content is trustworthy.
options: A word-processing spelling checker.
A printer’s paper sensor.
A spreadsheet’s sorting tool.
DNS.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.learningObjective: Apply responsible computing and information checks.
questions.prompt: What does HTTPS primarily add to an ordinary web connection?
questions.answer: Protection of the connection through TLS, rather than a guarantee that the site’s claims are truthful.
questions.explanation: Encryption and authentication of the connection are different from verifying every statement or offer on the site.
options: A guarantee that the site operator cannot deceive users.
A guarantee that the server and user device are free of malware.
Protection of the connection through TLS, rather than a guarantee that the site’s claims are truthful.
Automatic backup of every file on the user device.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.learningObjective: Distinguish communication functions and diagnose simple faults.
questions.prompt: When sending one email to several unrelated recipients, which field can hide their addresses from one another in the ordinary recipient display?
questions.answer: Bcc.
questions.explanation: Bcc conceals those recipients from the ordinary visible recipient list, though the sender and service still process the addresses.
options: Visible To addresses for every recipient.
Bcc.
Subject.
Cc.

questions.subject: Computer Studies

questions.prompt: Trace this pseudocode: total←0; FOR k←1 TO 4 inclusive: total←total+k; END FOR; OUTPUT total. What is output?
questions.explanation: The additions are 1+2+3+4 = 10.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.learningObjective: Trace and test explicitly stated algorithms.
questions.prompt: A field must contain an integer from 0 to 100 inclusive. Which input should a range-and-type validation reject?
questions.explanation: 105 is outside the stated range; the other listed integers satisfy it.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.learningObjective: Trace and test explicitly stated algorithms.
questions.prompt: Why should a program be tested with values exactly at accepted limits as well as ordinary values?
questions.answer: Boundary mistakes can remain hidden when only middle values are tested.
questions.explanation: Testing endpoints helps detect incorrect comparisons such as < where ≤ is required.
options: Ordinary tests can never be useful.
Only the final screen colour determines correctness.
Boundary mistakes can remain hidden when only middle values are tested.
Boundary inputs automatically prove every internal algorithm is correct.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.learningObjective: Evaluate storage recovery and maintenance methods.
questions.prompt: A user renames a text file from .txt to .jpg without converting its contents. What follows?
questions.answer: The name changes, but the contents do not automatically become a valid JPEG image.
questions.explanation: A filename extension can indicate intended type, but renaming alone is not content conversion.
options: The file is automatically decoded and rewritten into JPEG pixel data.
The name changes, but the contents do not automatically become a valid JPEG image.
All image programs must accept the renamed content as a valid JPEG.
Renaming alone cryptographically authenticates the file contents.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.learningObjective: Evaluate storage recovery and maintenance methods.
questions.prompt: Why is a successful restore test important for a backup plan?
questions.answer: It provides evidence that required data can actually be recovered in a usable form.
questions.explanation: A copied file or success message alone does not establish that recovery will work when needed.
options: It provides evidence that required data can actually be recovered in a usable form.
It guarantees there can never be a future device failure.
It means no further backups will ever be needed.
It replaces every need to identify which data was backed up.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.learningObjective: Apply responsible computing and information checks.
questions.prompt: An AI system produces a confident reference to a book that cannot be found in reliable catalogues. What is the most appropriate conclusion?
questions.answer: The reference needs verification; confident wording is not evidence that it exists.
questions.explanation: Generated language can contain fabricated or mistaken details, so source checking remains necessary.
options: Confidence proves the reference is authentic.
Every AI output is necessarily false.
The user should invent a publisher to complete the citation.
The reference needs verification; confident wording is not evidence that it exists.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.learningObjective: Explain computer components and data representation.
questions.prompt: Which description distinguishes an analogue representation from a digital one?
questions.answer: An analogue representation varies continuously, while a digital representation uses discrete values.
questions.explanation: This distinguishes representations, not a claim that all physical devices are purely one kind at every stage.
options: An analogue representation is defined by having only binary values.
Digital representations cannot describe measured physical quantities.
An analogue representation varies continuously, while a digital representation uses discrete values.
Analogue and digital refer only to the physical size of the equipment.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.learningObjective: Explain computer components and data representation.
questions.prompt: A touchscreen is an example of a device that can
questions.answer: provide visual output and receive touch input.
questions.explanation: The display and sensing functions support both directions of interaction.
options: perform no input function.
provide visual output and receive touch input.
only print hard-copy pages.
only store backups with no input or output.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.learningObjective: Explain computer components and data representation.
questions.prompt: Why can a CPU cache improve performance?
questions.answer: It can provide faster access to frequently or recently needed data and instructions.
questions.explanation: A cache reduces some slower memory accesses but does not eliminate the need for main memory or storage.
options: It can provide faster access to frequently or recently needed data and instructions.
Store all user files permanently after power is removed.
Replace the processor control unit.
Increase installed physical RAM capacity without adding memory.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.learningObjective: Explain computer components and data representation.
questions.prompt: An indexed image format allocates 4 bits to each pixel’s colour index. What is the maximum number of distinct indices?
questions.explanation: Four bits encode 2⁴ = 16 different index values.

questions.subject: Computer Studies

questions.explanation: The reference must point to a valid related record rather than create an enrolment for a non-existent student.
options: automatic correctness of every student’s name.
deletion of all student identifiers.
referential integrity.
a larger font size.

questions.learningObjective: Apply application concepts to defined tasks.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.learningObjective: Evaluate storage recovery and maintenance methods.
questions.prompt: In a sequential file organisation, records are typically processed
questions.answer: in an ordered sequence rather than accessed solely by a direct location calculation.
questions.explanation: Sequential processing follows an arrangement of records; it differs from describing every retrieval as direct access.
options: in an ordered sequence rather than accessed solely by a direct location calculation.
Only by a hash calculation that jumps directly to each record.
Only through a network protocol with no records.
Only by changing the file extension before every read.

questions.learningObjective: Distinguish communication functions and diagnose simple faults.
questions.prompt: A communication protocol is best described as
questions.answer: an agreed set of rules for exchanging data.

options: Only the physical material of the cable.
Only the storage capacity of a server.
A database key that identifies one learner.
an agreed set of rules for exchanging data.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.learningObjective: Evaluate storage recovery and maintenance methods.
questions.prompt: A computer’s cooling vents are blocked by dust. What is a plausible consequence?
questions.answer: Restricted airflow can contribute to overheating and unreliable operation.
questions.explanation: Cooling depends on suitable airflow; cleaning and servicing should follow safe, competent procedures.
options: No electronic device can be affected by temperature.
Blocked vents convert RAM into permanent storage.
Restricted airflow can contribute to overheating and unreliable operation.
Dust automatically increases all processor performance.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.learningObjective: Apply responsible computing and information checks.
questions.prompt: Which arrangement is most consistent with a suitable computer workstation?
questions.answer: A stable seat and screen position that support comfortable posture and clear viewing.
questions.explanation: Ergonomics concerns the user’s working arrangement rather than simply maximising screen brightness.
options: A requirement to twist continuously to see the screen.
A stable seat and screen position that support comfortable posture and clear viewing.
Cables across a walkway and a screen impossible to view comfortably.
A chair that cannot support the user at all.

questions.answer: Diamond.

options: Diamond.

Arrow used only as a flow line.
Parallelogram used for input/output.

questions.prompt: A program outputs “Pass” if score≥50; otherwise it outputs “Retry”. What is output for score=50?
questions.answer: Pass

options: Retry
Both outputs at once under the stated rule.
No output because equality is undefined.
Pass

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.learningObjective: Trace and test explicitly stated algorithms.
questions.prompt: A score of 65 is accidentally entered as 56. Both satisfy the permitted range 0–100. Why might a range check fail to detect the error?
questions.answer: Validation of permitted values is not the same as checking the value against the original source.
questions.explanation: A plausible but incorrectly copied value can pass a range check; verification is still needed.
options: Range checks can detect every transposition automatically.
Verification is impossible if a number is valid.
Validation of permitted values is not the same as checking the value against the original source.
All values inside the range are guaranteed to be the intended values.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.learningObjective: Apply application concepts to defined tasks.
questions.prompt: A school needs the same letter layout with a different learner’s name on each copy. Which word-processing feature is most directly suitable?
questions.answer: Mail merge using a template and a data source.
questions.explanation: Mail merge combines standard text with variable fields; the question concerns document preparation, not automatically sending messages.
options: Page orientation alone.
Mail merge using a template and a data source.
A spelling checker alone.
Manual independent copies with no shared template or data fields.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.learningObjective: Apply responsible computing and information checks.
questions.prompt: A photograph is publicly viewable online. What is the most responsible assumption before reusing it in a publication?
questions.answer: Public access does not itself establish permission; check the licence or obtain suitable permission.
questions.explanation: Visibility and reuse rights differ. The task does not assume a particular jurisdiction’s detailed exceptions.
options: Public access does not itself establish permission; check the licence or obtain suitable permission.
Every publicly viewable image is automatically free of all restrictions.
Changing the filename always transfers ownership.
Removing the creator’s name always makes reuse lawful.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.learningObjective: Trace and test explicitly stated algorithms.
questions.prompt: Trace this pseudocode and give x and total after each iteration: x←1; total←0; WHILE x<5: total←total+2*x; x←x+1; END WHILE. State final output total and explain what happens if the x increment is removed.
questions.answer: After successive iterations, (x,total) is (2,2), (3,6), (4,12), (5,20). Final total is 20. Without the increment, x remains 1, the condition stays true and the loop does not terminate under the stated model.
questions.explanation: Trace changing state in order; do not update x before using it unless the pseudocode says so.

markingGuide.description: Correct four successive state pairs.
Final total 20.
Explain unchanged x and non-termination if the increment is removed.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.learningObjective: Trace and test explicitly stated algorithms.
questions.prompt: Construct the complete truth table for a two-input NAND gate and explain how its result differs from AND. Use inputs 00, 01, 10 and 11.
questions.answer: For 00 the output is 1; for 01 it is 1; for 10 it is 1; for 11 it is 0. NAND is the negation of AND, so it gives the opposite binary output for every input pair.
questions.explanation: A complete table includes all four input combinations exactly once.

markingGuide.description: Correct output for each of four input pairs.
Explain negation of AND.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.learningObjective: Apply application concepts to defined tasks.
questions.prompt: A spreadsheet has daily pay in B2 and days worked in C2. A fixed bonus rate is stored in F1. Write a formula in D2 for B2*C2 plus a bonus equal to that product multiplied by F1. Make F1 stay fixed when copied down, and give the resulting formula in D3.
questions.answer: D2: =B2*C2*(1+$F$1). Copied to D3: =B3*C3*(1+$F$1). Equivalent formulas that add the base pay and bonus separately are also valid.
questions.explanation: The worker-row references change while the bonus-rate reference stays absolute.

markingGuide.description: Correct base-pay product.
Correct bonus application and total.
Use an absolute reference for F1.
Give the correct copied row-3 formula.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.learningObjective: Apply application concepts to defined tasks.
questions.prompt: A school stores learner details repeatedly in every subject-result row. A phone number is changed in some rows but not others. Explain the problem and propose a simpler linked-table design using a unique learner identifier.
questions.answer: Repeated learner details create redundancy and update anomalies. Store one learner row per unique learner identifier with the contact details, and store subject results separately with a reference to that identifier. Updating the learner contact once then avoids inconsistent copies in result rows.
questions.explanation: A suitable design separates learner facts from many result records while preserving a link; it does not remove necessary result data.

markingGuide.description: Explain redundancy and inconsistent updates.
Propose a learner table with unique identifier.
Propose linked result rows and explain the single update benefit.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.learningObjective: Evaluate storage recovery and maintenance methods.
questions.prompt: A shared folder is synchronised to another device. A user accidentally deletes files and the deletion synchronises too. Explain why synchronisation alone was insufficient and describe two recovery safeguards.
questions.answer: Synchronisation can copy changes, including deletion, rather than preserve an independent earlier state. Use versioned backups with suitable retention and a protected separate copy, and test restoring required files. Access controls and recovery records help prevent or investigate further loss.
questions.explanation: Two identical current folders are not necessarily two recoverable historical copies.

markingGuide.description: Explain propagation of deletion.
Explain two suitable safeguards linked to recoverable earlier states or protection.
Explain a restore test or retained recovery evidence.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.learningObjective: Distinguish communication functions and diagnose simple faults.
questions.prompt: A computer can reach a known local service by IP address but cannot resolve its hostname. Other conditions are unchanged. Identify a likely area to investigate and describe a sensible check before replacing hardware.
questions.answer: Investigate name resolution, including the configured DNS service or local name records. Compare a known correct hostname, check relevant settings and test whether other names resolve. Since IP access works, a complete physical-network failure is not established.
questions.explanation: The symptoms narrow the investigation but do not prove a single cause; check evidence before replacing a cable or adapter.

markingGuide.description: Identify name-resolution/DNS investigation.
Describe two relevant checks or comparisons.
Explain why successful IP access weakens a total hardware-failure claim.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.learningObjective: Explain computer components and data representation.
questions.prompt: A raw uncompressed image is 100 pixels wide and 80 pixels high at 8 bits per pixel. Ignoring headers and palettes, calculate size in bits, bytes and KiB, where 1 KiB=1024 bytes. Explain why an actual saved file may have a different size.
questions.answer: Size = 100×80×8 = 64,000 bits = 8,000 bytes = 7.8125 KiB. Headers, palettes, metadata or compression can change the saved file size relative to the raw pixel-data calculation.
questions.explanation: The stated representation excludes padding and other overhead; file format matters in real storage.

markingGuide.description: Calculate 64,000 bits.
Convert to 8,000 bytes.
Convert to 7.8125 KiB.
Explain a valid file-format or compression difference.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.learningObjective: Apply application concepts to defined tasks.
questions.prompt: A long school report has manually enlarged headings, repeated blank lines and inconsistent page starts. Explain how paragraph styles, proper page breaks and an automatic contents feature could improve maintainability.
questions.answer: Styles apply consistent heading formatting and document structure. Proper page breaks control new pages without fragile runs of blank lines. Heading-based contents can be updated when sections or pagination change.
questions.explanation: The response should link each feature to editing and updating the report, not claim that visual formatting alone makes the content accurate.

markingGuide.description: Explain styles and consistent structured headings.
Explain stable page breaks.
Explain an updateable contents list.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.learningObjective: Trace and test explicitly stated algorithms.
questions.prompt: Design tests for a score input that must be an integer from 0 to 100 inclusive. Give one ordinary valid value, both valid endpoints, one value below range, one above range and a non-integer input. State expected acceptance or rejection and why these tests are not proof of the whole program’s correctness.
questions.answer: Examples: 50 accepted; 0 accepted; 100 accepted; −1 rejected; 101 rejected; 1.5 or non-numeric text rejected. These check representative type/range and boundary behaviour but do not test every processing path, storage action or output elsewhere in the program.
questions.explanation: Credit equivalent values meeting the requested categories. Distinguish successful input checks from proof of every program property.

markingGuide.description: Ordinary valid value and both accepted endpoints.
Rejected below-range, above-range and non-integer cases.
Explain a limitation of the test set.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.learningObjective: Apply responsible computing and information checks.
questions.prompt: A staff member needs a list of learners eligible for a club, but requests an unrestricted export containing home addresses and unrelated family details. Explain two privacy or access concerns and propose a proportionate information-sharing approach.
questions.answer: The export includes more personal information than needed and may give access beyond the staff member’s role. Provide only authorised fields relevant to eligibility, apply appropriate access controls and retain a record of the approved purpose and disclosure.
questions.explanation: This is an educational data-handling scenario, not a statement of every jurisdiction’s legal requirements. A legitimate task does not justify unrestricted data access.

markingGuide.description: Explain excess/unnecessary data concern.
Explain role or access-authorisation concern.
Propose a relevant minimal authorised dataset and traceable sharing arrangement.
